name: DecoBlocks – Speech Bubble, Sticker, Table of Contents & Highlight Blocks
author: LUX Digest

sections.description:
DecoBlocks is a post decoration plugin for the WordPress Block Editor (Gutenberg) and the Classic Editor. It adds speech bubble, quote box, section box, highlight, sparkle text, glow box, divider, custom bullet list and character sticker blocks, plus an automatic table of contents (TOC) — without writing any CSS.

  • Speech bubble blocks – filled or outline, left or right, for dialogue and asides
  • Quote and section boxes – several built-in styles for quotes, notes and callouts
  • Text highlight and sparkle text – make key sentences stand out
  • Table of contents – generated automatically from your headings
  • Character stickers – install sticker packs by independent illustrators and place them in your posts
  • Works everywhere – native blocks in the Block Editor, shortcodes with toolbar buttons in the Classic Editor
  • Multilingual – the editor and admin screens are in English, with Korean and Japanese translations included

Most WordPress posts read like documents. DecoBlocks is built for the posts that should read like you — the ones where a reader stops scrolling, actually feels something, and sticks around.

Plain, information-only writing is easy to skim, easy to summarize, and increasingly easy to replace. What’s harder to replace is a post with a real voice behind it — the small human touches (a sticker at just the right moment, a highlighted aside, a speech bubble that sounds like you talking) that no template and no AI-generated draft quite gets right. That’s the gap DecoBlocks fills: the same kind of expressive stickers you already use every day in chat apps, brought into your blog posts — a visual rhythm for pacing emotion across a page that WordPress has never quite had.

The practical effect, when it’s used well: readers stay on the page longer, they’re more likely to comment or come back, and your writing simply feels more like someone’s, not something’s. DecoBlocks doesn’t promise a ranking boost — no plugin honestly can — but posts that keep people reading and coming back are exactly the kind of signal search engines are built to reward.

Character stickers are the centerpiece: install packs made by independent illustrators (Insert Sticker block, or the Get from Marketplace tab) and drop them into your posts to punctuate a feeling — surprise, warmth, a laugh — the same way a well-placed sticker does on a personal blog. Alongside them, DecoBlocks gives you a full set of ready-made design blocks — speech bubbles, styled quote boxes, section boxes, custom bullet icons, text highlights, an auto-generated table of contents, glow effects, and an animated firework decoration — all without writing a single line of CSS, as native blocks (Gutenberg) or shortcodes (Classic Editor).

Whether you call it post decoration, blog design, writing decoration, or content styling, DecoBlocks is built to make your posts beautiful, readable, and — most of all — recognizably, humanly yours.

Free Features

  • Speech bubble (filled / outline, left/right)
  • Section box (solid / shadow / dashed)
  • Custom bullet list icons (check / star / heart / arrow / point)
  • Text highlight (yellow / green)
  • Auto-generated table of contents
  • Sparkle text effect
  • Glow box (pulse effect)
  • Auto-repeating firework decoration (gold / rainbow colors, adjustable particle count and timing)
  • Quote block with multiple built-in styles (classic / vertical bar / line frame / big quotation marks / sticky note / corner frame – the last two show a plain, undecorated version for free; the colored, decorated version needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Speech bubble Pastel style (plain gray version for free; the colored pastel + avatar image needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Glow box Twinkle style (glows the same as Pulse Glow for free; the sparkling star decoration needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Divider block with multiple built-in styles (solid / dashed / dotted / diamond / arrow / diagonal slash / tick mark – the last four show a plain, undecorated version for free; the gradient, shadowed version needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Custom color palette and the option to hide the “Powered by” credit — both free, no upgrade needed
  • Independent heading tag (H2–H6, or plain text) and font size choice on every text block — your choice, whether or not you want it picked up by search engines
  • Works in both the Block Editor and the Classic Editor

3D Style Upgrade (paid add-on, 2.99 $ / month subscription)

  • Pastel speech bubble style and avatar images
  • Sticky-note and corner-frame quote styles
  • Diamond / arrow / diagonal-slash / tick-mark divider ornaments
  • Multi-color confetti firework bursts
  • Rainbow shine text, glowing twinkle-star box, and animated gradient highlight sweep
  • Genuine 3D depth effects (shadows, embossing, elevation) layered on top of the styles above

External services

This plugin connects to a marketplace server operated by the plugin author (store.luxdigest.com) for the optional sticker-pack feature. No data is sent to this server as part of normal plugin use (decoration blocks, shortcodes, TOC, etc.) — only the specific actions below trigger a connection, and only when you actively use them:

  • Browsing/installing sticker packs (“Get from Marketplace” tab in the Insert Sticker block): sends your site’s language (ko/en/ja, informational only — the server returns every pack regardless) and, when installing a pack, your license key and site URL (home_url()), to fetch the pack list and download the pack’s image files. Endpoints: GET /packs, GET /packs/{slug} — used only when you open this tab or click Install.
  • Sticker pack license lookup (DecoBlocks → License Keys): sends the license key you paste to identify which pack it belongs to, then reuses the pack install flow above. Endpoint: GET /license-lookup — used only when you click “Add”.
  • Purchase links: the “Get 3D Styles” and pack purchase buttons link out (in a new browser tab) to /buy-3d and /buy/{slug} on the same marketplace server to start the 3D Style Upgrade subscription or buy a sticker pack. No data is sent automatically — this only opens when you click a purchase button yourself.

The DecoBlocks 3D Style Upgrade is a separate, independent plugin, not distributed through WordPress.org — this free plugin never downloads, installs, or connects to anything on its behalf. It is offered as a monthly subscription directly on store.luxdigest.com; after subscribing you receive an email with a link to download the plugin’s zip file, which you install manually like any other plugin (Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin). All license verification for that upgrade happens inside that separate plugin, not here.

This service is operated by the same developer as this plugin. Terms of Service: https://store.luxdigest.com/terms-of-service/ — Privacy Policy: https://store.luxdigest.com/privacy-policy/ — Refund Policy: https://store.luxdigest.com/refund-policy/ — Contact: https://store.luxdigest.com/contact/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/decoblocks, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Look for the “DecoBlocks” category in the block inserter, or use the toolbar buttons in the Classic Editor.
sections.faq:
Does this work with the Classic Editor?

Yes. Every block also has a matching shortcode with a toolbar button and Quicktags button for the Classic Editor.

Will this slow down my site?

No. Styles and scripts are only loaded when needed, and all animations are lightweight, dependency-free JavaScript.

Is there a speech bubble block for WordPress?

Yes. DecoBlocks includes a Speech Bubble block (filled or outline, left or right) for the Block Editor and a matching shortcode for the Classic Editor.

Can I add a table of contents to my posts?

Yes. The Table of Contents block builds a list of links from the headings of the post automatically.

Does it work with any theme?

DecoBlocks uses standard WordPress blocks, so it works with block themes and classic themes. If a theme sets very dark backgrounds, choose light colors for the effects in the block settings.

Is DecoBlocks available in Korean and Japanese?

Yes. Korean (ko_KR) and Japanese (ja) translations of the editor and admin screens are included and follow your site or user language.
sections.changelog:
2.44.58

  • Improved: the readme title, tags, short description and description were rewritten so the plugin is easier to find in the WordPress plugin directory (speech bubble, table of contents, highlight, sticker blocks); FAQ entries added.

2.44.57

  • Fixed: on sites with a dark background (black themes), text inside DecoBlocks effects became unreadable. The Highlight text turned black (browsers color black by default) on a black page, and text inside the white-background cards (Speech Bubble Outline/Soft, Section Box, Glow Box, Table of Contents) took the theme’s light text or heading color, so it was white-on-white or gold-on-white. The stylesheet now decides text color itself wherever it paints its own background (dark ink on light cards; the Filled Speech Bubble picks white or black from the fill color; Post-it uses dark ink on the paper color) and lets text on transparent backgrounds (Highlight, Dashed Section Box, most Quote Box styles, Firework caption) follow the site’s own text color, so dark sites get light text and light sites get dark text. Highlight color bands become more transparent when the text is light so the text stays readable on them. Selectors are made more specific instead of using !important so a theme’s “content h2 { color }” rule no longer overrides them.
  • Fixed: the Filled Speech Bubble could show a theme heading color (e.g. dark text on the default #111 fill) even on light sites.
  • Colors you choose for effects (bubble fill, box/glow title, sparkle, divider) are unchanged. Note: a dark color such as the default #111111 is still dark on a black page – pick a light color for those effects on black sites.

2.44.56

  • Compatibility with multilingual plugins (Polylang and its forks): the bundled Korean/Japanese translations are registered as the translation path, so they are reloaded correctly when the plugin switches the front-end language after WordPress has started.

2.44.55

  • Added bundled Korean (ko_KR) and Japanese (ja) translations for all editor and admin strings, including the block editor sidebar (JavaScript). The interface follows the site/user language; language packs from translate.wordpress.org take precedence when installed.
  • Fixed: a few block editor strings written with \u escapes (e.g. “Loading…”) could not be matched by translation files.
  • Added translators comments for strings with placeholders.

2.44.54

  • Fixed: when a Quote Box style (Classic/Big Quotation Marks/Vertical Bar/Line Frame/Post-it/Corner Frame) had a source/attribution filled in, the whitespace above the title and the whitespace below the attribution could look unequal even though top and bottom padding are the same number – most often when the title is rendered as a heading tag (H2-H6), because the theme’s own default heading margin wasn’t always fully cancelled by this stylesheet’s margin reset. Both the reset (.dbk-quote__content > *:first-child / *:last-child) and the attribution’s own bottom margin are now !important, so the space above the first line and below the last line is always exactly the box’s own padding – the same whether an attribution is filled in or left empty. The 10px gap between the title and the attribution itself is unchanged (that’s an intentional inner gap, not the outer top/bottom whitespace this fixes).
  • Changed: all 6 Quote Box styles’ padding increased by 1.5x, by explicit request – Classic 18/34 → 27/51, Big Quotation Marks 20/44/24/52 → 30/66/36/78, Vertical Bar 24/0/24/30 → 36/0/36/45, Line Frame 24/32 → 36/48, Post-it 24/28 → 36/42, Corner Frame 24/28 → 36/42. Corner Frame’s 3D padding also scaled the same way (36/40 → 54/60); the matching add-on update ships in 3D Style Upgrade 1.4.2.

2.44.53

  • Changed: Quote Box – Vertical Bar (10-3-1/10-3-2) top/bottom padding increased from 8px to 24px, matching Classic/Big Quotation Marks/Post-it – by explicit request, to make the whitespace above/below the text noticeably generous like the other quote styles, not just technically bug-free. Left padding (30px, for the color bar) and right padding (0) are unchanged. Verified live on a published post: the site now loads dbk-frontend.css?ver=2.44.53 and the block’s computed top/bottom padding is 24px.
  • Verified: confirmed on a real published luxdigest.com post (via the browser’s actual computed styles, not just reading the source) that 2.44.51/2.44.52’s Post-it, Vertical Bar and Big Quotation Marks padding fixes are correctly live – computed padding matched the CSS exactly (Post-it 24px/28px, Vertical Bar 8px/30px before this release’s change, Big Quotation Marks 20px/24px/52px) and the correct plugin/add-on versions were the ones actually loaded. If a site still shows old spacing after updating, it’s a caching issue (browser cache or a page-cache plugin/CDN), not a plugin bug – clear the site’s page cache and hard-refresh the browser.

2.44.52

  • Fixed: 2.44.51’s fix for Post-it/Corner Frame’s editor-vs-published padding (below) turned out to be incomplete on at least one real site – raising the selector to two classes wasn’t always enough to beat the theme’s own blockquote padding rule, only shrinking the gap instead of closing it. All 6 Quote Box styles’ base padding (Classic, Big Quotation Marks, Vertical Bar, Line Frame, Post-it, Corner Frame – 10-1-1/10-2-1/10-3-1/10-4-1/10-5-1/10-6-1) now use !important instead, the same technique this stylesheet already used for this exact element’s margin and border (see the “10-0” shared rule). This wins regardless of how specific the theme’s own selector is. Corner Frame’s 3D padding (36px 40px) needs the matching update in the 3D Style Upgrade add-on (1.4.1) so it still overrides Corner Frame’s own now-!important base padding when 3D is on; Post-it, Classic, Big Quotation Marks, Vertical Bar and Line Frame need no add-on change since the add-on never sets their padding.
  • Correction: 2.44.51’s changelog entry said the 3D Style Upgrade add-on “never sets padding” for Post-it or Corner Frame. That’s true for Post-it, but wrong for Corner Frame – the add-on does set a larger 36px 40px padding for Corner Frame’s 3D form specifically.

2.44.51

  • Fixed: Quote Box – Post-it (10-5-1) and Corner Frame (10-6-1) could show generous padding above/below the text in the editor but noticeably tighter padding on the published page. Both are rendered as a real <blockquote> tag, and their padding rule used a single-class selector (.dbk-quote--postit / .dbk-quote--corner-frame) – on sites whose theme sets its own padding on blockquote with a class+tag selector (e.g. .entry-content blockquote), that theme rule is more specific and wins on the published page only, since the editor never loads the theme’s front-end stylesheet. Raised both selectors to the two-class .dbk-quote.dbk-quote--* form, matching the fix already applied to Classic, Big Quotation Marks, Vertical Bar and Line Frame. This does not affect the 3D Style Upgrade add-on, which never sets padding for these two styles and already uses two-class-or-higher selectors of its own.
  • Changed: the settings sidebar of Quote Box – Big Quotation Marks (10-2-1/10-2-2), Line Frame (10-4-1/10-4-2), Sticky Note (10-5-1/10-5-2) and Corner Frame (10-6-1/10-6-2) now shows Text tag → Color → Text Align at the top, the same order as Classic and Vertical Bar and every other DecoBlocks block. Font Size stays in its own panel below. No style or output changes.

2.44.49

  • Changed: all prices are now shown as “number $” (e.g. “5.99 $”) everywhere – sticker pack prices and Buy buttons in the block editor’s marketplace tab and in the Classic Editor sticker list now match the 3D Style Upgrade’s “2.99 $ / month”.

2.44.48

  • Changed: the 3D Style Upgrade is now a monthly subscription (2.99 $ / month), so every place in the editor and admin screens that described it as a one-time purchase has been updated – the price buttons now read “2.99 $ / month”, and “Purchase Required to Publish”, “Buy 3D Style Upgrade”, “Already purchased?” and similar wording now say subscribe/subscription. Sticker packs are still one-time purchases and their wording is unchanged.
  • Fixed: on My Purchases, a site whose 3D Style Upgrade subscription has ended was told “no license key entered yet” even though the key is already saved. It now says the subscription has ended and that resubscribing turns 3D back on with the same key, with a Resubscribe button.
  • No block, style or CSS changes.

2.44.47

  • Changed: Speech Bubble (1-1-1) Outline and Pastel styles no longer recolor the text – the chosen color now goes only into the bubble’s shape (Outline: border and tail; Pastel: a light tint of the chosen color as the background). Text keeps the theme’s default color and can still be changed with the editor’s own text color option. Filled is unchanged.
  • Changed: Speech Bubble 3D (1-1-2) now casts its shadow toward the bottom-right (top-left light source), tinted with the chosen color, like Section Box 3D.
  • Changed: Quote Box – Classic 3D (10-1-2), Vertical Bar 3D (10-3-2, including the bar’s own shadow) and Corner Frame 3D (10-6-2) shadows are now tinted with the chosen color. Their depth and position are unchanged.
  • Fixed: Quote Box – Big Quotation Marks 3D (10-2-2) now has a bottom-right drop shadow (same values as Post-it 3D), instead of shading that read as coming from the top-left.
  • Added: Quote Box – Post-it (10-5-1) and Post-it 3D (10-5-2) now use the chosen color as the note’s paper color (a pastel of that color, and for 3D the same diagonal light-to-deeper gradient in that color). With the default color, the existing yellow note is unchanged.
  • The matching published-page changes ship in 3D Style Upgrade add-on 1.3.11.

2.44.46

  • Changed: Section Box 3D (2-1-2, Solid/Dashed) frame line is now a barely-there 1px line instead of the base style’s 2px line in full color. It uses your chosen color at very low opacity – lightest on the top and left (the lit side), slightly stronger on the right and bottom (the shadow side). The colored bottom-right drop shadow from 2.44.45 is unchanged, and the base Section Box (2-1-1) keeps its 2px border. The matching published-page change ships in 3D Style Upgrade add-on 1.3.10.

2.44.45

  • Fixed: Section Box 3D (2-1-2) ignored the color you picked. Its shadow was hard-coded black, and the editor preview never passed the --dbk-box-color variable to the block (only the border color), so the shadow and title always used the default black. The 3D shadow is now tinted with your chosen color while keeping the Section Box’s own shape: a top-left light source with the shadow cast toward the bottom-right (it does not glow on all sides like the Glow Box). The matching published-page fix ships in 3D Style Upgrade add-on 1.3.9.
  • Changed: Highlight (4-1-1) colors are now Yellow, Lime and Orange. Green was changed to lime (existing highlights that used green now show as lime automatically – the color="green" value is kept for compatibility) and Orange was added, in the block editor, on published pages, and in the Classic Editor menu.
  • Changed: Sidebar order for Speech Bubble (1-1), Section Box (2-1), Highlight (4-1), Sparkle Text (6-1), Glow Box (7-1), Firework Effect (8), Quote Box – Classic (10-1) and Quote Box – Vertical Bar (10-3), including their 3D versions: the “Text tag” (H2-H6) control now comes first, then Color, then Text Align (for blocks that have it), followed by the remaining settings. Font size stays in its own panel below. Other Quote Box styles are unchanged.
  • Fixed: Table of Contents (5) now calculates hierarchical numbers – H2 headings are numbered 1, 2, 3 and H3 headings under an H2 are numbered 2-1, 2-2, and so on – and adds them to each item (data-toc-num). The 3D version’s number badges (3D Style Upgrade add-on 1.3.9) now show these numbers instead of numbering every item flatly as 1, 2, 3, 4.

2.44.44

  • Fixed: Quote Box – Corner Frame’s 3D editor preview (10-6-2) had almost no depth – only a small filter: drop-shadow that also blurred a shadow onto the quote text. Its shadow now matches Quote Box – Post-it 3D (10-5-2) exactly, with a consistent top-left light source: a drop shadow cast toward the bottom-right, a highlight along the inner top edge, and soft shading along the inner bottom edge. Only the shadow changed – the corner brackets’ shape, thickness, color, position and padding are unchanged. The matching published-page fix ships in 3D Style Upgrade add-on 1.3.8.

2.44.43

  • Reverted: Quote Box – Classic’s 3D editor preview (10-1-2) is restored exactly to its 2.44.40 styling (shadows and bracket shading), undoing the 2.44.41 and 2.44.42 changes. No other block or style is changed. The black at the bottom ends of the brackets on published pages actually came from the 3D Style Upgrade add-on’s own stylesheet, and is fixed there in add-on v1.3.6.

2.44.42

  • Fixed: 2.44.41 made Quote Box – Classic’s 3D preview (10-1-2) look flat. It drew the bracket lines with border-image, which this stylesheet deliberately avoids (it renders thinner and blurrier than intended), and it relied only on the existing faint box shadow for depth. Reverted border-image and rebuilt the depth with a consistent top-left light source: a white highlight on the top-left edge, plus a short, darker contact shadow and a wider soft shadow cast toward the bottom-right. Each bracket line now also gets its own drop shadow that follows the line shape (not a box-shaped shadow, so the brackets don’t look like a second floating layer). The bracket lines still contain no black: the lit faces (top, outer left) use a lighter tint of your chosen color, and the faces away from the light (bottom, outer right) use your exact color.

2.44.41

  • Fixed: Quote Box – Classic’s 3D preview (10-1-2) mixed 45% black into the bottom edge of each “[ ]” bracket (border-bottom-color) to fake depth, which made the bottom ends of the brackets look like dirty black stubs – especially visible on the published page. The bracket lines themselves no longer contain any black: they are now drawn as a single-color vertical gradient in your chosen color only (lighter tint at the top fading into your exact color at the bottom). The depth/shading is kept – it still comes from the quote box’s existing soft drop shadow, which is unchanged. Bracket shape and thickness are unchanged. The 3D Style Upgrade add-on (paid, separate plugin) needs a matching update if it ships its own copy of this rule for published pages.

2.44.40

  • Fixed (performance/reliability): the “Table of Contents” block’s render callback was calling do_blocks() + do_shortcode() on the entire post content a second time, inside the normal single-pass block rendering that WordPress already performs for the_content. Any post containing a TOC block therefore had every block in it rendered twice on every single frontend page view (no caching across requests), roughly doubling CPU cost for that page and re-running any other plugin’s render_block filters twice per request – a likely cause of slow page loads, intermittent errors, and (under concurrent traffic on limited PHP-FPM workers) full site unavailability. The TOC block now uses the same lightweight placeholder mechanism the [decobl_toc] shortcode already used (fill in the actual table of contents once, in the the_content filter, after normal rendering has already finished) – producing the identical table of contents with no extra rendering pass.

2.44.39

  • Fixed: Highlight block’s 3D variation (4-1-2) showed a different inserter icon (“A” text-color icon) than its own base block (4-1-1, pencil icon), even though they’re the same block family (base vs. 3D-addon form) – making them look unrelated in the block inserter list. The 3D variation now reuses the same pencil icon as the base block.
  • Fixed: Divider Line’s Dashed (11-2-1/11-2-2) and Dotted (11-3-1/11-3-2) styles used the same generic dash (“minus”) icon as Solid (11-1-1/11-1-2), so all three looked identical in the block inserter even though they render very differently on the page (Dashed is a thick dashed line, Dotted is a row of round dots). Each style now gets its own custom icon that reflects its actual line pattern, while each style’s base/3D-addon pair still shares one unified icon – so all three Divider Line styles are now visually distinguishable from each other, and easy to tell apart from Solid.

2.44.38

  • Fixed: Table of Contents (5-1/5-2) items looked like links (hand cursor on hover) but clicking one never actually jumped to that section. The TOC always built links like #dbk-toc-anchor-0, but nothing ever added a matching id="dbk-toc-anchor-0" to the actual heading on the page – so every TOC link pointed at a destination that didn’t exist anywhere in the page, whether the TOC came from the block or the [decobl_toc] shortcode. Headings now get that id automatically (and if a heading already has its own id – e.g. set manually via the core “HTML anchor” field – that existing id is used instead of overwriting it), so clicking a TOC entry actually scrolls to that section now.

2.44.37

  • Fixed: Sparkle Text’s block editor preview never actually applied the Speed setting or the chosen Color at all – the editor-only preview code always rendered with a hardcoded empty/fixed class list and never passed your chosen color down to the element, so no matter what you picked for Speed or Color in the sidebar, the editor canvas kept showing a fixed fast animation in the default gold color. This is why the 2.44.36 CSS fix below didn’t visibly change anything – the CSS was correct, but the editor was never attaching the classes/color for that CSS to act on in the first place. The published page’s own renderer was never affected by this (it already built the classes and color correctly), only the in-editor preview was broken. Fixed the editor preview to actually pass your Speed and Color choices through, for both the base effect and its 3D preview.

2.44.36

  • Fixed: Sparkle Text 3D preview (6-1-2) speed control (Slow/Normal/Fast) had no visible effect – the CSS never defined an animation-duration override for the slow/fast classes on the 3D variant (and the base non-3D effect was missing them entirely), so every speed setting played at the same fixed rate. Rewired the animation so the speed setting is actually applied, for both the base effect and its 3D preview.
  • Changed: Sparkle Text 3D preview’s gradient used to spend most of its length on currentColor (your text’s normal color, usually black) with your chosen sparkle color only flashing through briefly – so most of the time it looked like plain dark text with a stray glint, not a colorful effect. Rebuilt the gradient to use your chosen color across its full length, with the white glint passing over it, so the color you picked is what’s actually emphasized instead of being drowned out. The 3D Style Upgrade add-on (paid, separate plugin) needs its matching v1.3.5 update installed for this to appear on a licensed, published site – see that plugin’s own changelog.

2.44.35

  • Fixed: Quote Box – Line Frame’s 3D preview (10-4-2) did not actually match what was requested. Earlier revisions to this CSS block (mentioned in code comments as “confirmed after several rounds of real user feedback”) replaced the original double-line request with a single thin offset line per side and no shadow – but that history was inaccurate, and the published result did not match what was actually asked for. Rewrote this block correctly: a crisp, evenly-thick double line at both the top and the bottom (built from a hard-stop gradient rather than the native border-style: double, which cannot always split small widths into equal whole pixels), combined together with a soft drop shadow across the whole quote box, exactly as originally requested. The 3D Style Upgrade add-on (paid, separate plugin) needs its matching v1.3.4 update installed for this to appear on a licensed, published site – see that plugin’s own changelog.

2.44.34

  • Changed: Quote Box – Corner Frame’s 3D editor preview (10-6-2) used to show plain thin brackets in your chosen color with a simple shadow, but the actual 3D Style Upgrade add-on (paid, separate plugin) has always drawn something noticeably more elaborate on a licensed, published post – thicker diagonal-gradient brackets (light tone fading into your chosen color) with a soft drop shadow. That meant the editor preview undersold what a purchase actually delivers. Updated the editor preview to match the add-on’s actual output exactly, so what you see while writing is what you get after publishing. Still uses only your chosen color (as a gradient of it, never a different color) – no rendering change for sites without the add-on installed.

2.44.33

  • Fixed: Highlight (4-1-1/4-1-2) and Sparkle Text (6-1-1/6-1-2) each render as their own Gutenberg block, and in the editor they visually stack one per line because the block editor wraps every block’s preview in its own container <div>. But their PHP output (the part that actually reaches the published page) only ever returned the bare inline <mark>/<span> element itself, with no such wrapper – so several Highlight or Sparkle blocks placed one after another, which looked like separate lines while editing, collapsed onto a single run-on line once published, since consecutive inline elements with no wrapper flow together regardless of how they were laid out in the editor. Wrapped each block’s frontend output in its own <div> (decoblocks/highlight → .dbk-highlight-wrap, decoblocks/sparkle → .dbk-sparkle-wrap) so the published page now stacks them exactly as shown in the editor. The [decobl_highlight]/[decobl_sparkle] Classic Editor shortcodes – which are meant to highlight/sparkle a few words in the middle of a sentence – are untouched and still render inline with no wrapper, since they share the same rendering engine but are invoked separately from the block.

2.44.32

  • Added: Glow Box 3D’s multi-color rainbow pulse is no longer the only “3D” look. A new “3D Glow Color” dropdown (shown once the 3D preview is turned on) lets you choose between “Use My Color” (default) and “Rainbow”. “Use My Color” makes the glow a single-hue neon effect built from whatever color you’ve picked for the box – pick red, the glow is red; pick purple, the glow is purple – layered at a few different blur/opacity levels for a genuine neon-sign look, instead of always being a fixed multi-color rainbow. If the box’s color is left at its default black, the 3D glow falls back to a bright orange instead of a barely-visible black glow. “Rainbow” keeps the existing gold/orange/green cycling glow from 2.44.31 for anyone who prefers it. Also available in the Classic Editor shortcode as [decobl_glow rainbow3d="1"].

2.44.31

  • Fixed: Quote Box – Classic’s 3D preview added a whole-element ambient shadow in 2.44.30 to connect the shading through the middle, but each bracket end (::before/::after) still kept its own separate drop shadow on top of that, so the two brackets visually “floated” one layer above the box beneath them instead of reading as one continuous surface. Removed the brackets’ own individual box-shadow – their light/dark top-to-bottom border coloring is enough on its own, layered under the single whole-element shadow, so it now reads as one consistent raised surface end to end.
  • Redesigned: Glow Box 3D’s gold/orange/green glow (2.44.30) only ever changed in brightness, never in color balance – all three color layers grew and shrank together at the exact same ratio, so the closest/brightest gold layer always visually dominated and the whole effect just read as “a fixed yellow glow,” not a rainbow. The pulse animation is rebuilt so each color takes a turn being the largest, brightest layer in a rotating sequence (gold → orange → green → back to gold), so the glow now visibly shifts between colors over time instead of only pulsing in intensity. Animation length increased from 2s to 3s so the color shift reads as a smooth transition rather than a flicker.

2.44.30

  • Fixed: Quote Box – Classic’s 3D preview only shaded the two bracket ends (::before/::after) – the flat area between them (where the quote text sits) had no shading at all, so the box read as “raised only at both edges, flat in the middle” instead of one continuously lifted shape. Added a soft ambient box-shadow to the element itself (on top of the brackets’ own existing shading), so the whole quote box now reads as a single continuously raised surface, brackets included.
  • Fixed: Quote Box – Vertical Bar’s 3D bar still showed a hint of black at its base even after 2.44.27’s color-mix() fix, because the gradient’s darkest stop was mixed 60% color / 40% black – dark enough to read as near-black on lower-saturation colors – and the bar’s own ambient drop shadow was strong enough to visually blend into that dark end. Lightened the gradient’s dark stop to 78% color / 22% black and softened the ambient shadow, so the bar’s base now reads as a darker shade of the chosen color instead of black bleeding through.
  • Changed: Glow Box 3D’s rainbow pulse used a pink/purple/teal palette that read as dark and muddy rather than a true “rainbow” glow. Replaced with a brighter gold/orange/green combination (the green matches the plugin’s own default accent color for consistency), matching the warmer, brighter palette originally intended for this effect.

2.44.29

  • Changed: the block inserter’s item names now show this plugin’s internal CSS block-reference number instead of the generic “(DecoBlocks)” suffix – e.g. “Speech Bubble (1-1-1)” for the free version and “✨ Speech Bubble (1-1-2, 3D)” for its 3D preview, “Quote Box – Classic (10-1-1)” / “(10-1-2, 3D)”, and so on for every block. This is purely a label change for easier reference between the block list and the CSS source (assets/css/dbk-frontend.css is organized under matching numbered comment headers, e.g. “10-1-1″/”10-1-2”) – no rendering, styling, or attribute behavior changed. The “Purchase Required to Publish” notice on unlicensed 3D items is unchanged, just now prefixed with its reference number.

2.44.28

  • Fixed: Section Box and Glow Box’s “Title” field could never actually become a real H2-H6 heading, even though the block’s Typography panel let you choose a heading tag for the body content. The title itself was always hard-coded to render as a plain <div> (in both the PHP renderer and the block editor’s own preview), so the Table of Contents block – which scans the page’s real HTML for <h2>/<h3> tags – could never pick it up, no matter what a writer intended the title to be. Added a dedicated “Title heading level” dropdown (Default / H2 / H3 / H4 / H5 / H6) that appears once a title is entered, for both Section Box and Glow Box, in the block editor, and wired the same option into the [decobl_box title_tag="h2"] / [decobl_glow title_tag="h2"] Classic Editor shortcodes. Titles marked H2 or H3 are now automatically picked up by the Table of Contents block, exactly like any other H2/H3 in the post. Leaving this at its default keeps rendering a plain, non-heading <div> exactly as before, so already-published posts are unaffected. Also added a margin: 0 reset to the title’s CSS so switching it to a real heading tag doesn’t introduce the browser’s default heading margin around it.

2.44.27

  • Redesigned: Quote Box – Classic’s box-with-a-border shape from 2.44.26 turned out to be visually indistinguishable from Section Box’s own plain rectangle. Rebuilt as a pair of classic open bracket shapes (“[” on the left, “]” on the right, each a 3-sided corner stroke) wrapping the quote text instead – a silhouette that doesn’t overlap with Section Box, Vertical Bar, or the Big Quotation Marks style. 3D keeps this exact bracket shape and only shades it (lighter top edge, darker bottom edge, soft drop shadow).
  • Redesigned: Quote Box – Vertical Bar’s 3D preview now also lifts the entire quote box with a soft shadow (the same technique used for Section Box/Classic), in addition to keeping its own bar – previously only the bar itself got extra shading, not the box around it.
  • Fixed: Quote Box – Vertical Bar’s 3D bar showed a visible black tint mixed into the color whenever a non-default (non-black) quote color was chosen, because the light/shadow effect was built from separate white/black translucent overlay layers stacked on top of the color. Rebuilt using color-mix() (the same technique already used for the Highlight gradient) so the bar is a single continuous shade of the chosen color, light to dark, with no separate black layer showing through. The bar’s outer black ring outline is also removed for the same reason; only an ordinary ambient drop shadow (which is expected to be dark regardless of the element’s own color) remains.
  • Fixed: Glow Box 3D’s multi-color pulsing glow was still shown next to the plain single-color border from the free-tier style (which defaults to black), making the two look disconnected. The border is now hidden (made transparent, same box size) whenever the 3D preview is active, so only the glow itself defines the edge.

2.44.26

  • Redesigned: Quote Box – Classic’s free/base shape was still a single left border, which didn’t visually read as a distinct style from Quote Box – Vertical Bar and made the two hard to tell apart at a glance. The base style itself is now a bordered box on all four sides (not just a left edge) – this is an explicit, user-directed change to the free-tier CSS (normally left alone). The 3D preview keeps this exact same box shape and only adds soft light/shadow depth on top of it – no separate accent bar, and no decorative quotation-mark glyphs (removed – they duplicated the dedicated Quotation Marks style and weren’t wanted here).
  • Fixed: Quote Box – Line Frame’s 3D top/bottom lines sat flush against the box’s own padding edge, which read as neither clearly attached nor clearly floating (“어정쩡한” was the word used). The lines are now offset 6px outward from the box, giving them visible breathing room from the quote text so they read as a deliberate floating frame instead of an ambiguous half-border.
  • Changed: Quote Box – Sticky Note’s …

short_description: Speech bubble, quote box, highlight, table of contents and sticker blocks for the Block Editor and Classic Editor. No CSS needed.
description:
DecoBlocks is a post decoration plugin for the WordPress Block Editor (Gutenberg) and the Classic Editor. It adds speech bubble, quote box, section box, highlight, sparkle text, glow box, divider, custom bullet list and character sticker blocks, plus an automatic table of contents (TOC) — without writing any CSS.

  • Speech bubble blocks – filled or outline, left or right, for dialogue and asides
  • Quote and section boxes – several built-in styles for quotes, notes and callouts
  • Text highlight and sparkle text – make key sentences stand out
  • Table of contents – generated automatically from your headings
  • Character stickers – install sticker packs by independent illustrators and place them in your posts
  • Works everywhere – native blocks in the Block Editor, shortcodes with toolbar buttons in the Classic Editor
  • Multilingual – the editor and admin screens are in English, with Korean and Japanese translations included

Most WordPress posts read like documents. DecoBlocks is built for the posts that should read like you — the ones where a reader stops scrolling, actually feels something, and sticks around.

Plain, information-only writing is easy to skim, easy to summarize, and increasingly easy to replace. What’s harder to replace is a post with a real voice behind it — the small human touches (a sticker at just the right moment, a highlighted aside, a speech bubble that sounds like you talking) that no template and no AI-generated draft quite gets right. That’s the gap DecoBlocks fills: the same kind of expressive stickers you already use every day in chat apps, brought into your blog posts — a visual rhythm for pacing emotion across a page that WordPress has never quite had.

The practical effect, when it’s used well: readers stay on the page longer, they’re more likely to comment or come back, and your writing simply feels more like someone’s, not something’s. DecoBlocks doesn’t promise a ranking boost — no plugin honestly can — but posts that keep people reading and coming back are exactly the kind of signal search engines are built to reward.

Character stickers are the centerpiece: install packs made by independent illustrators (Insert Sticker block, or the Get from Marketplace tab) and drop them into your posts to punctuate a feeling — surprise, warmth, a laugh — the same way a well-placed sticker does on a personal blog. Alongside them, DecoBlocks gives you a full set of ready-made design blocks — speech bubbles, styled quote boxes, section boxes, custom bullet icons, text highlights, an auto-generated table of contents, glow effects, and an animated firework decoration — all without writing a single line of CSS, as native blocks (Gutenberg) or shortcodes (Classic Editor).

Whether you call it post decoration, blog design, writing decoration, or content styling, DecoBlocks is built to make your posts beautiful, readable, and — most of all — recognizably, humanly yours.

Free Features

  • Speech bubble (filled / outline, left/right)
  • Section box (solid / shadow / dashed)
  • Custom bullet list icons (check / star / heart / arrow / point)
  • Text highlight (yellow / green)
  • Auto-generated table of contents
  • Sparkle text effect
  • Glow box (pulse effect)
  • Auto-repeating firework decoration (gold / rainbow colors, adjustable particle count and timing)
  • Quote block with multiple built-in styles (classic / vertical bar / line frame / big quotation marks / sticky note / corner frame – the last two show a plain, undecorated version for free; the colored, decorated version needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Speech bubble Pastel style (plain gray version for free; the colored pastel + avatar image needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Glow box Twinkle style (glows the same as Pulse Glow for free; the sparkling star decoration needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Divider block with multiple built-in styles (solid / dashed / dotted / diamond / arrow / diagonal slash / tick mark – the last four show a plain, undecorated version for free; the gradient, shadowed version needs the 3D Style Upgrade)
  • Custom color palette and the option to hide the “Powered by” credit — both free, no upgrade needed
  • Independent heading tag (H2–H6, or plain text) and font size choice on every text block — your choice, whether or not you want it picked up by search engines
  • Works in both the Block Editor and the Classic Editor

3D Style Upgrade (paid add-on, 2.99 $ / month subscription)

  • Pastel speech bubble style and avatar images
  • Sticky-note and corner-frame quote styles
  • Diamond / arrow / diagonal-slash / tick-mark divider ornaments
  • Multi-color confetti firework bursts
  • Rainbow shine text, glowing twinkle-star box, and animated gradient highlight sweep
  • Genuine 3D depth effects (shadows, embossing, elevation) layered on top of the styles above

External services

This plugin connects to a marketplace server operated by the plugin author (store.luxdigest.com) for the optional sticker-pack feature. No data is sent to this server as part of normal plugin use (decoration blocks, shortcodes, TOC, etc.) — only the specific actions below trigger a connection, and only when you actively use them:

  • Browsing/installing sticker packs (“Get from Marketplace” tab in the Insert Sticker block): sends your site’s language (ko/en/ja, informational only — the server returns every pack regardless) and, when installing a pack, your license key and site URL (home_url()), to fetch the pack list and download the pack’s image files. Endpoints: GET /packs, GET /packs/{slug} — used only when you open this tab or click Install.
  • Sticker pack license lookup (DecoBlocks → License Keys): sends the license key you paste to identify which pack it belongs to, then reuses the pack install flow above. Endpoint: GET /license-lookup — used only when you click “Add”.
  • Purchase links: the “Get 3D Styles” and pack purchase buttons link out (in a new browser tab) to /buy-3d and /buy/{slug} on the same marketplace server to start the 3D Style Upgrade subscription or buy a sticker pack. No data is sent automatically — this only opens when you click a purchase button yourself.

The DecoBlocks 3D Style Upgrade is a separate, independent plugin, not distributed through WordPress.org — this free plugin never downloads, installs, or connects to anything on its behalf. It is offered as a monthly subscription directly on store.luxdigest.com; after subscribing you receive an email with a link to download the plugin’s zip file, which you install manually like any other plugin (Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin). All license verification for that upgrade happens inside that separate plugin, not here.

This service is operated by the same developer as this plugin. Terms of Service: https://store.luxdigest.com/terms-of-service/ — Privacy Policy: https://store.luxdigest.com/privacy-policy/ — Refund Policy: https://store.luxdigest.com/refund-policy/ — Contact: https://store.luxdigest.com/contact/
